source.title: The BUTTER Zone: An Empirical Study of Training Dynamics in Fully Connected Neural Networks
source.authors: C. Tripp; J. Perr-Sauer; Lucas Hayne; Monte Lunacek; Jamil Gafur

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own scaling-related results on finite-data MLP tasks and presents them as preliminary, empirical relationships requiring qualification; it also tests architecture-shape effects and extrapolation in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper cites language-model scaling laws but those cited results are not rows. It does not test language-model pretraining loss, token or compute scaling, or compute-optimal allocation. Rows below cover its own MLP loss-versus-parameter fits, extrapolation, and shape comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own large grid of fully connected MLPs on 13 finite tabular/image tasks. It reports minimum test loss against parameter count, fits an analytic form, extrapolates it to other sweeps, and compares shapes and aspect ratios. That is a new setting with results bearing on V2, V4 and V5. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is roughly right. It should add that the authors state their dataset 'corroborates' scaling-law findings (power-law scaling with parameters; shape matters little) for MLPs and finite datasets. They call their analytic fits preliminary, purely empirical and based on a small fraction of the data.
record.recipe_differences: Unlike language-model pretraining scaling studies, this work surveys fully connected MLPs trained on finite tabular regression and classification tasks, using test-loss sweeps over parameters, depth, shape, and epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported relationships use task- and shape-specific constants; test performance varies at deep-and-narrow and wide-and-shallow aspect ratios.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The scaling analysis is preliminary, uses only a small fraction of the dataset, and is described as solely empirical. The extrapolation result is qualitative and shown for connect_4 MLPs; the paper cautions against generalizing beyond its finite set of tasks and hyperparameter combinations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results left out. Cited scaling-law results from other studies are not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: Extrapolation across orders of magnitude; quantitative prediction error; language models; tasks other than connect_4.
Language-model architecture details; anything beyond MLP width, depth and shape.
Image or video generative models, fine-tuning and transfer; data-size or compute scaling (only parameter count is fitted).
Not tested: no exponents are reported or compared across fitting choices or published laws.

missing.what: Depth effect at matched settings: a flat optimum between 3 and 7 layers overall, but the best depth varies by task (mnist best shallow, 201_pol best deep). This bears on V4.

record.verdict_notes: MLP-on-tabular results are linked to V4 and V2 even though the claim originates in language models. Researchers should weigh them as a different kind of system. The authors' claimed corroboration of power-law scaling in data size and compute is not backed by their own fits, which cover parameter count only.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss and power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute when the other quantities are not bottlenecks.
Extrapolation is tested only for MLPs on the connect_4 task, not language models or runs orders of magnitude larger in the language-model setting.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token allocation trend is tested.
The paper studies MLP depth, width, and shape on its selected tasks; it does not test language-model architecture details.
Tests finite-data MLP tasks, not image or video models, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream-task performance or downstream predictability from pretraining loss is tested.
Task- and shape-specific fits are reported, but published-law disagreement, compute-optimal split sensitivity, and systematic bending away from a single power law in language models are not tested.

rows.subject: BUTTER MLPs (aggregate across reported tasks and shapes)
rows.operation_detail: Fit analytic functions to minimum median test loss, minimizing epoch, and descent slope as functions of parameter count.

conditions.value: 7 datasets examined in the preliminary analysis
4 shapes examined; fits shown for rectangular networks

rows.measure: Minimum median test loss versus number of trainable parameters
rows.value: The fitted form for minimum test loss is log(ϕmin) = c(log(σ) − ς0)^−p + φ; the authors describe an approximate power-law relationship. Constants are task- and shape-specific.
rows.note: The analysis is explicitly preliminary and empirical, and the authors say it uses only a fraction of the dataset. The reported relationship is for minimum test loss in finite-data MLP tasks, not pretraining loss.
rows.check: Drop the V7 link. The constants are never reported, so nothing shows exponents shifting with setup or published laws disagreeing. Keep V5 as partial: Eq. 2 is a power law in log(params) with an offset, log(ϕmin)=c(log σ−ς0)^−p+φ, not the standard L∝N^−α. The loss is the minimum over epochs from 3000-epoch training on finite data. Fits are shown for 7 tasks at depth 3.

rows.subject: Rectangular MLPs on connect_4 (aggregate over repetitions)
rows.operation_detail: Apply fits from the Primary Sweep to estimate minimum-loss locations in the 300 Epoch and 30k Epoch sweeps.
rows.measure: Minimum test loss and its location as parameter count and training epoch vary
rows.value: Equations 1 and 2 give 'promisingly reasonable estimates' of minimum test-loss locations in the additional sweeps.
rows.note: The prediction outcome is described qualitatively; the figure overlays the fit and sweep results.
rows.check: Drop the V5 link; this row is about extrapolation only. The test sets are the 300 Epoch sweep (up to 2^27 params vs 2^25 in the Primary Sweep, about 4x) and the 30k Epoch sweep (smaller params, longer training). That is not orders of magnitude. The result is qualitative ('promisingly reasonable estimates'), on connect_4 only.

rows.subject: BUTTER MLPs (aggregate across reported tasks)
rows.operation_detail: Compare test-loss performance across network width-to-depth aspect ratios.

conditions.value: Wide range spanning many orders of magnitude

rows.value: Networks achieve good test losses across a wide range of width-to-depth aspect ratios.
rows.note: Figure 2 displays normalized, log-scaled test losses; the accompanying text describes the broad-range result.

source_check.locator_found: Section IV-A, paragraph discussing Figure 2: broad aspect-ratio result explicitly describes four tasks.

rows.subject: BUTTER MLPs (aggregate across reported tasks)
rows.operation_detail: Compare test-loss performance across network width-to-depth aspect ratios.

conditions.value: Deep and narrow; also wide and shallow

rows.value: Performance degrades for deep and narrow networks and, to a lesser extent, for wide and shallow networks.
rows.note: The authors report the degradation qualitatively; Figure 2 shows the normalized test-loss values.

rows.subject: BUTTER MLPs (aggregate across tasks and topologies)
rows.operation_detail: Compare marginal performance across network shapes.
rows.value: Network shape had a negligible impact on training performance.
rows.locator: Section IV-A; Figure 1 and Appendix B, Figures 9–12
rows.note: This statement concerns training performance; the separate test-loss aspect-ratio results are recorded in r3 and r4.
rows.check: Fig. 1 plots median minimum test loss and epochs to reach it, so the measure is test loss, not training performance as the record says. The shape comparison is a marginal averaged over parameter counts and tasks.

source_check.correct: The prose uses 'training performance', but Figure 1 measures median minimum test loss and median epochs to reach it. Figures 9–12 show median test loss and its relative interquartile range. Record the measure as generalization performance and epochs to minimum test loss.
source_check.locator_found: Section IV-A; Figure 1 caption; Appendix B, Figures 9–12 captions.
source_check.problem: The recorded measure inherits imprecise prose wording; the supporting figures measure test performance.

relationships.condition: Rectangular depth-3 MLPs on connect_4; Primary Sweep fit applied to the 300 Epoch and 30k Epoch sweeps
relationships.reason: The fitted Eqs. 1–2 give reasonable estimates of where minimum loss falls in held-out sweeps (r2). This is qualitative and only about 4x beyond the fitted parameter range.
relationships.display_finding: Fitted equations reasonably estimated minimum-loss locations in additional sweeps extending about 4× beyond the fitted parameter range.

relationships.condition: Finite-data MLPs, minimum test loss over 3000 epochs, 7 tasks, rectangular depth 3
relationships.reason: Loss falls with parameter count with diminishing returns. But the fitted form is a power law in log(params) with offsets, not the standard power law (r1).
relationships.display_finding: Minimum test loss decreased with diminishing returns, following an offset power law in log parameter size rather than the standard parameter power law.
